speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; to begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any fever or other systemic signs?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Staphylococcal Scalded Skin Syndrome (SSSS).

The patient is a 50-year-old female presenting with a triad of cutaneous blistering on the forearm, oral ulcers causing pain on eating, and genital ulcers causing dyspareunia. Her recent exposure to hiking in the woods and the specific constellation of symptoms strongly suggest a disseminated infection, possibly from a Group A Strep or Staph aureus source encountered during her hike, rather than a drug reaction given the timeline. Given the severity of the mucosal involvement and the blistering, I need to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes. I will request a culture and blood work. REQUEST TEST: Blood Culture, CBC, and CRP. REQUEST TEST: Tzanck smear from the forearm blister.
